passages.t: ‘Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion’, and the hills robed with joy
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song” (verse 1). This is a song of thanks in three movements.

First, God who forgives. “Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion” (verse 1). He listens: “O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You” (verse 2). “When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions” (verse 3).

Second, God who rules the world. “You formed the mountains by Your power” (verse 6). “You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves, and the tumult of the nations” (verse 7). “You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy” (verse 8).

Third, God who sends rain. “You attend to the earth and water it” (verse 9). “You soak its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth. You crown the year with Your bounty” (verses 10 and 11). The whole land seems to sing: “the hills are robed with joy” (verse 12), and the valleys “shout in triumph; indeed, they sing” (verse 13).
passages.hearers:
Israel lived by rain. Egypt and Babylon had great rivers to water their fields. Israel did not. It needed the autumn rains to soften the ground for ploughing and the spring rains to ripen the grain. God promised, “I will provide rain for your land in season, the autumn and spring rains” (Deuteronomy 11:14). A failed rainy season meant hunger.

The Canaanites around Israel gave the credit for rain to Baal, the storm god. This psalm gives it all to Israel's God.

No occasion is named, but the psalm sounds like a harvest festival, when vows made during the growing season were paid (verse 1).

The first line has a word heard in Psalm 62. Word for word it reads, ‘To You, silence is praise.’ Some hear in it a hushed waiting before God, before the singing starts.
passages.later:
Paul told the people of Lystra that God “has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons” (Acts 14:17). Jesus said that God “sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous” (Matthew 5:45).

Isaiah compares God's word to rain that does not return without watering the earth (Isaiah 55:10-11).
passages.asks:
Notice the order. Forgiveness comes first, then creation, then harvest. The God who makes the wheat grow is the same God who deals with our sin.

Next time you eat bread, think of verse 11: ‘You crown the year with Your bounty.’ Rain, soil, seed and sun are not machines. They are gifts. Who do you thank for them?
